reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds. Listing refunds first.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (orders 192, 193, 194 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the order list to identify the customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the orders identify three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance before recording any payout, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 33841 matches my own check (orders 190 and 193 total 43422, less the 9581 refund on order 193). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme and birch both match my own arithmetic from the orders and refunds. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance before recording any payouts.

Cobalt's net balance of 18779 matches my check (orders 192 and 195 total 21927, less the 3148 refund on order 192). All three balances agree with my arithmetic and the refunds table matches Alpha's report, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 33841 is recorded. Birch's net balance is 35184, which matches my check (orders 191 and 194 total 40664, less the 5480 refund on order 194). Recording birch's payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, whose net balance of 18779 matches my check (21927 in orders less the 3148 refund), so I'll record that payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched my own check against the orders and refunds, so the batch is complete.
